facts.text: The applicant was born in 1983 and lives in Istanbul.

anchor.surface_text: 6.  The applicant was born in 1983 and lives in Istanbul.

facts.text: The applicant owns and runs a website on which he publishes his academic work and his views on various topics. The website was created using the Google Sites service.

anchor.surface_text: 7.  The applicant owns and runs a website (http://sites.google.com/a/ahmetyildirim.com.tr/academic/) on which he publishes his academic work and his views on various topics. The website was created using the Google Sites website creation and hosting service (http://sites.google.com/).

facts.text: On 23 June 2009, the Denizli Criminal Court of First Instance ordered the blocking of a specific website under section 8(1)(b) of Law no. 5651 as a preventive measure in criminal proceedings against the site’s owner accused of insulting Atatürk.

anchor.surface_text: 8.  On 23 June 2009, under section 8(1)(b) of Law no. 5651 on regulating Internet publications and combating Internet offences, the Denizli Criminal Court of First Instance ordered the blocking of the website http://sites.google.com/site/kemalizminkarinagrisi/benimhikayem/at...

facts.text: On 23 June 2009, a copy of the blocking order was sent to the Telecommunications and Information Technology Directorate (TİB) for execution under section 8(3) of Law no. 5651.

anchor.surface_text: 9.  On the same day, under section 8(3) of Law no. 5651, a copy of the blocking order was sent to the Telecommunications and Information Technology Directorate (“the TİB”) for execution.

facts.text: On 24 June 2009, at the request of the TİB, the Denizli Criminal Court of First Instance ordered the blocking of all access to Google Sites under section 8 of Law no. 5651, as the offending website owner lived abroad and had no server certificate.

anchor.surface_text: 10.  On 24 June 2009, at the request of the TİB, the Denizli Criminal Court of First Instance varied its decision of 23 June and ordered the blocking of all access to Google Sites under section 8 of Law no. 5651. The TİB had indicated that this was the only means of blocking the offending website, as its owner did not have a server certificate and lived abroad.

facts.text: The TİB implemented the order of 24 June 2009 by blocking all access to Google Sites, preventing the applicant from accessing his own website.

anchor.surface_text: 11.  The TİB, implementing the order of 24 June 2009, blocked all access to Google Sites and the applicant was thus unable to access his own website.

facts.text: On 1 July 2009, the applicant applied to have the blocking order of 24 June 2009 set aside in respect of his website, arguing that the measure barred access to his site which had no connection with the offending website and that only the offending website should have been blocked.

anchor.surface_text: 12.  On 1 July 2009 the applicant applied to have the blocking order of 24 June 2009 set aside in respect of his website. He pointed out that he used the website regularly in order to publish his academic work and his opinions on various topics, and that the measure had barred all access to his site, which had no connection with the offending website.

facts.text: The applicant submitted a copy of the webpage displayed when trying to access his website, showing a warning that the TİB had applied the blocking order issued by the Denizli Criminal Court of First Instance on 24 June 2009.

anchor.surface_text: In support of his request, the applicant furnished the court with a copy of the webpage which appeared when he tried to access his own website. The following warning was displayed: “The Telecommunications and Information Technology Directorate has applied the order issued by the Denizli Criminal Court of First Instance on 24 June 2009 in respect of this website (sites.google.com) as a preventive measure.”

facts.text: On 13 July 2009, the Denizli Criminal Court dismissed the applicant’s application to set aside the blocking order, considering that blocking access to Google Sites was the only means of blocking the offending website.

anchor.surface_text: 13.  On 13 July 2009 the Denizli Criminal Court dismissed the applicant’s application. Referring to a recommendation issued by the TİB, it considered that the only means of blocking access to the offending website, in accordance with the blocking order, had been to block access to the Google Sites service, which had hosted the content complained of.

facts.text: On 25 April 2012, the applicant informed the Court that he was still unable to access his website, although the criminal proceedings against the owner of the offending website had been discontinued on 25 March 2011 due to inability to determine the accused's identity and address.

anchor.surface_text: 14.  The applicant wrote to the Court on 25 April 2012 informing it that he was still unable to access his website even though, as far as he understood it, the criminal proceedings against the owner of the offending website had been discontinued on 25 March 2011 because of the impossibility of determining the identity and address of the accused, who lived abroad.
Article 10 of the Convention

concepts.interpretation: The Court found a violation of Article 10 due to the blocking of access to the applicant's website, which constituted an interference with freedom of expression not justified by law or necessary in a democratic society.

1.  Declares admissible the complaint concerning the interference with the applicant’s freedom to receive and impart information;

anchor.surface_text: 2.  Holds that there has been a violation of Article 10 of the Convention;

holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court concluded that the blocking of access to the applicant's website constituted an unjustified interference with his freedom of expression under Article 10, due to lack of legal safeguards, disproportionality, and absence of consideration of Convention principles by domestic courts.
